description: Three-wheeled open-sided auto rickshaw with a single front wheel, handlebar steering and a rear bench under a curved canopy.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Three-wheeled auto rickshaw, single front wheel with handlebar steering, rounded front cowl and headlamp, open sides with a curved canopy roof over a rear passenger bench, chrome bar frame and rear luggage rack Materials: Glossy two-tone enamel with chrome trim, polished stainless canopy edge, scuffed rubber floor mat, worn vinyl bench, exhaust soot at the rear.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.90. 4,514/4,800 triangles (asset ceiling raised from 4,000 with the arithmetic in notes), 4/4 draw calls, 4/4 materials, 4/8 unique geometries, two 256 px canvases at 0.7 MB, factory 74 ms. Turntable: enclosed background is the open cabin, allowed on measurement.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at 1.28 x 1.95 x 2.90 m against a declared 1.40 x 1.95 x 2.90; the proxy reads the body at 1.17 and the rear track at 1.30 (1 : 0.662 : 0.449), so the width is built to the measurement and the declaration is the tolerance ceiling. Every longitudinal station is read off the side depth map in real metres (scratch/tuk-tuk/_ev/stations.py).
featureReviews.notes: The deleted build was a flat lens canopy on chrome sticks over a box tub, with a slab nose and disc wheels. The depth map shows what the plate implies: a domed roof whose rear rolls DOWN (1.90 @ -0.72, 1.80 @ -1.00, 1.57 @ -1.13) into an enclosed rear quarter with a vertical tail at z -1.16, a roof lip cantilevered to z +0.84 over the driver, a concave leg shield bellying to z 1.00, and a front pillar at the half-door's rear edge -- the proxy puts that pillar at z +0.07 and the plate crop wins.

featureReviews.evidence: One C-section shell (roof band with a 9 cm shoulder fillet, a 3 cm cross-width crown and 28/22 cm plan roundings, tail wall, floor pan), quarter-panel strips with the arch cut, a half door in a chrome frame whose rear leg hooks down as an armrest, a chrome pillar from the door's rear-top corner to the roof lip, a broad C-pillar with the chrome rail running up its opening edge and round the roof lip, bench with a leaning back, mat, rear window, green tube basket.
featureReviews.notes: Three faults came out of the renders rather than any gate. The yellow belt stripe vanished into the panel: first because the arch flare stood over it (arch dropped to hub height, stripe raised under the belt), then because a plan rounding projects only the vertices inside its corner zone, so a strip's single earcut cap triangulation ran from an unprojected front vertex to a projected tail vertex and tilted the whole face 6 cm inward -- the shell's floor edge was dragged 4 cm inside the panels the same way. Fixed with a vertex at every tangent station and by cutting the panel and stripe into 6-8 cm slices through the corner. The roof-lip rail also rode 1.5 cm above the lip at the front and read as a pale sliver.

featureReviews.evidence: Leg shield tumbled 32% to the cowl top and plan-rounded r 0.10, bellying to z 1.00 at y 0.75 off the depth map; yellow centre band 12 mm proud with a tilted chrome-bezel lamp buried 4 cm into the shield and three grille slots; headstock nacelle lathe leaning 23 degrees; bars, black grips, left mirror; fender hugging the tyre 37-168 degrees with chrome beads; chrome edge trim down both shield sides continuing into the floor rail.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's shield is broader and more concave than a 0.50 m sweep can carry without a second profile; the band and lamp placement are read off crop-nose.png.

featureReviews.evidence: Three instanced pressed-steel wheels: hub cap, dished centre, vent ring, rim lip and a tread whose lugs alternate two tones per segment, 19 points at 12 segments. Tyre held on chroma at #3a3226; hub #9a958c measured off the plate's front wheel.
featureReviews.notes: 12 segments is the floor for a 0.54 m wheel; 14 cost 228 triangles across the three instances for no visible gain at prop distance.

featureReviews.evidence: Green authored #3f8562 as the inverse of the harness's 0.83 side transfer against the plate's #387558 lit flank; yellow #e8b418 against #e2ad0e. Band on the shield, stripe under the belt rail wrapping the tail corners on the corner slices.
featureReviews.notes: Stripe visible end to end on the 090/270 frames and wrapping to the tail on 180.

name: Tuk-tuk
notes: Sized on the Bangkok tourist tuk-tuk rather than the larger cargo samlor. Open-sided, so the interior bench and floor are visible from every angle and cannot be faked with a closed shell. No destruction groups: the canopy is a welded bar frame, not a removable assembly. Triangle ceiling raised 4,000 -> 4,800 on the 2026-09-02 rebuild: the class default was set when the prop shipped as 3,244 triangles of slabs and disc wheels, which the user deleted; the rebuild measures 4,514, of which three instanced 12-segment pressed-steel wheels are 1,368 (19-point lathe x 12 x 2 x 3) and the C-section shell, quarter panels and corner slices 1,600. Draw calls, materials and unique geometries stay at 4 / 4 / 4.
